SaniTap · plantation tracker · desk analysis · Aug 2026

Cascade Plantation Growth History

Domaine de la Cascade, Anosy (−24.994, 46.912). 176 usable satellite scenes 2009–2026 (65 Landsat, 111 Sentinel-2) plus 134 Sentinel-1 radar passes, analysed per performance stratum: the mapped good zone (0.56 ha) vs the poor remainder (17.6 ha).

The three questions, answered:
1. Can satellites reconstruct the growth history? Yes — a continuous 17-year record (fig 1) shows establishment-era NDVI (~0.60) rising through 2014–2017 to a stable canopy plateau, with phased greening visible in the chronology map (fig 6). The record is censored at 2009: 12.3 ha was already vegetated then (earlier planting or prior cover).
2. Can they distinguish good from poor? Yes, decisively — the strata separate from 2012 (Cohen's d 0.83) and in every Sentinel-2 year 2016–2025 (d 0.6–2.0, p < 10⁻¹⁶). The discrimination is seasonal: the gap triples in Nov–Jan (fig 2b) when the poor stratum browns on exhausted soil moisture while the streamside good zone stays green — direct field validation of the suitability tool's wetter-is-better premise, and the MRV recipe: monitor in Nov–Dec.
3. Is the xlsx curve consistent with this plantation? No — and that is the point. The poor stratum stands at an estimated 1–11% of the modelled year-15 biomass; the model curve describes a good site (like the good zone, 33–119% of model), not an average one. Site selection is not a refinement of the project — it is the difference between the model being right and wrong.
Boundary discrepancy — needs your decision. The corrected boundary is 18.1 ha against the historically quoted ~26 ha. Fig 7 shows spectrally similar blocks outside the boundary (orange). Caveat: NDVI similarity alone cannot tell plantation from natural woodland, and most of the 84.6 ha of "compatible" area east of the site is clearly natural vegetation. The blocks worth checking against high-res imagery are the ones hugging the boundary: NE corner (~1.5–2.4 ha) and the southern lobes (~0.5–1 ha each). If any are yours, re-run the editor and I'll update every figure.

1 · NDVI history by stratum

Both strata start near 0.60–0.65 under Landsat (30 m), rise through 2014–2017, and plateau at ~0.84 (good) vs ~0.78 (poor). Two anomalies are honest features of the record: 2015 is the Landsat→Sentinel-2 hand-off (few scenes, mixed sensors), and 2026 shows the good zone dropping to 0.72, below the poor stratum — either recent cutting in the good zone or an artifact of the thin partial-year composite. Do you know of 2026 harvesting there?

2 · Seasonal behaviour — the discrimination mechanism

The classic wet-minus-dry amplitude metric (fig 2, in the repo) is muddied by cyclone-season cloud sampling; the month-by-month gap climatology above is the clean view. Sep–Jan is when desk monitoring can grade site quality; Mar–Jul it cannot (gap 0.02–0.04, within noise of a single scene).

3 · Radar structure check

Sentinel-1 VH backscatter runs ~0.62 dB higher over the good zone in recent years — consistent with denser woody structure — but C-band saturates at roughly 50–100 t/ha of biomass, so radar corroborates rather than quantifies here.

4 · The plantation developing, year by year

Recovered chronology: 12.3 ha already green at the 2009 series start (censored — planted earlier or pre-existing cover), then phased greening of ~1.5 ha (2011), ~0.8 ha (2012), ~1.9 ha (2013), ~1.5 ha (2015). The good zone's own signal is instructive: in 2011 it read lower than the poor stratum (d = −0.67) — freshly planted into cleared ground — and overtook everything by 2012. Treat years as ±1: Landsat pixels are 30 m and the onset threshold is a desk heuristic.

5 · Pixel-level mixture (your contamination caveat, confirmed)

45% of poor-stratum pixels exceed the good zone's median in the 2024–26 composite — the right tail you predicted from unmapped scattered good clumps, plus optical saturation once even a thin-culm canopy closes. Stratum medians remain strongly separable; single pixels are not a reliable per-clump verdict.

6 · Standing biomass — ranges, not points

Whole site18.13 ha— 67.0–795.4124.1–1473.0 vs 4,406–5,508 t if fully as modelled

How these numbers are built (satellite indices cannot weigh stems — anchors are structural): (a) culm-level allometry — bamboo culm mass scales roughly with diameter² (per village-bamboo allometries for B. balcooa and congeners, Nath et al. 2009, Biomass & Bioenergy 33:1188–96; Kaushal et al. bamboo biomass studies), so a 1–4 cm "fishing rod" carries ~0.3–1.5 kg dry against 5–10.3 kg for a proper culm (xlsx: 7 kg avg, 10.3 kg Tana sample); (b) the xlsx per-clump curve (608 kg dry at year 15) as the "performing as modelled" ceiling. Clump density assumed 350–500/ha. Uncertainty is ±40–50% and skewed: NDVI saturation makes thin-culm stands look better than they are; Sentinel-1 keeps the structural floor honest.

One-day field calibration protocol (MadAvance / Cascade) — collapses the ranges to ~±15–20%:
· 16 plots of 10 × 10 m: 12 in the poor stratum (4 per NDVI tercile — I can supply the stratified plot coordinates), 3 in the good zone, 1 straddling the boundary.
· Per plot: count clumps; on 3 clumps per plot count all culms and tape/calliper the DBH of 5 culms; measure 2 culm heights (pole or clinometer).
· If cutting is permitted: weigh 2–3 freshly cut culms across diameter classes (spring scale) for a local wet-mass check (moisture 0.46 assumed otherwise).
· Phone-GPS each plot corner; photos along one diagonal.
That is ~20 min per plot for a crew of three — one field day.

7 · Verdicts

DIY satellite MRV: credible, with stated limits. Free imagery reliably tracks canopy establishment, detects phase timing, grades site quality seasonally (Nov–Dec window), and flags disturbance (the 2026 good-zone dip). It cannot measure culm diameter — the fishing-rod problem is structural, and satellites see leaves, not stems: without the field anchor, optical data would have called this plantation a success.

xlsx curve: keep it as the good-site trajectory it demonstrably is (the good zone plausibly sits at 33–119% of it), but a site-quality multiplier belongs in any whole-portfolio projection: this 15-year site holds roughly 1–18% of its fully-modelled standing stock. RiverGuard's benchmark-anchored site selection exists precisely to keep new plantings out of this graph's red band.

Next instrument: if structure monitoring matters, a drone photogrammetry flight is the right buy — canopy height + gap fraction at clump scale for the whole 18 ha in one afternoon (the planting rows already resolve in Bing's z18 basemap). It still will not weigh culms; pair it with the one-day plot protocol above and both questions close.

Caveats & sources

Strata as corrected by AM (16 Aug 2026); poor stratum contains unmapped good clumps (right-tail contamination, fig 5) and its quality varies bad-to-worse. Good zone is 0.56 ha as drawn (~2–3 ha was described — extend in the editor if under-drawn, stats will sharpen). Boundary precision beyond ~10 m is immaterial to these results (analysis pixels are 10 m S2 / 30 m Landsat; good-zone Landsat medians rest on ~6 pixels, hence pre-2016 noise). GEDI: 16 L2A granules intersect the area but footprint data needs NASA Earthdata auth — skipped (time-boxed). Chronology censored at 2009. 2026 composites are partial-year.
